biography.plain_text: Franz Koch is an Austrian entrepreneur who founded Koch International and cofounded Koch Media with Klemens Kundratitz. His businesses expanded from recorded music into computer games, software and film distribution. He sold his controlling interest in Koch Media to THQ Nordic, while his family retained its book publishing and property interests.

long_biography.plain_text:
Franz Koch built his recording business around giving regional musicians access to a fully equipped studio. At Elbigenalp, artists performing German-language folk music could record under conditions more commonly offered to pop acts. His group also handled publishing, printed the record packaging, manufactured discs and cassettes, and distributed recordings internationally.

When Koch sold the European music operations to Universal in 2002, he explained that digital distribution would require investment on a scale better supported by a large company. He remained attached to the folk repertoire but judged the necessary spending too risky. The transaction excluded the group's American operations and Austrian logistics facility.
